Figures are quoted as the page states them; the page's own death-toll and 'heard' figures vary between sections (36,417 recorded by the Dutch, 'more than 120,000' by some; 3,110 km Perth vs 3,600 km Alice Springs), and the 'heard' claim uses only the 1883-eruption section's figures. The page gives no outline of the pre-1883 island, so none is drawn: the map shows today's coast with labels and figures only. The point is the page's infobox coordinate for Krakatoa (one point for the archipelago, approximate). Perth and Rodrigues are not points in the research and are not marked.

claims.text: Krakatoa is a caldera in the Sunda Strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra; the Krakatoa archipelago comprises four islands.
At the time of the 1883 eruption the island of Krakatoa was 9 km long by 5 km wide.
On 27 August 1883 a series of four huge explosions almost destroyed the island; the eruption destroyed two-thirds of the island of Krakatoa.
The explosions were heard 3,110 km away in Perth, Western Australia, and on the island of Rodrigues near Mauritius, 4,800 km away.
The death toll recorded by the Dutch authorities was 36,417, although some sources put the estimate at more than 120,000.

On 29 December 1927 a submarine lava dome showed eruptions and a new island volcano rose above the waterline a few days later; that island and the two that followed were quickly eroded away, and a fourth island, Anak Krakatau ('child of Krakatoa' in Indonesian), broke water in August 1930 and produced lava flows more quickly than the waves could erode them.
In late 2011 Anak Krakatau had a radius of roughly 2 km and a highest point of about 324 metres above sea level, growing five metres each year.
In 2017 the height of Anak Krakatau was reported as over 400 m above sea level; following a collapse in December 2018 the height was reduced to 110 meters.
On 22 December 2018 an eruption of Anak Krakatoa collapsed the main volcanic cone and the southwestern flank, causing a deadly tsunami with waves up to five meters in height making landfall.
Periodic eruptions continued into September 2023 as well as into July and September 2026.
